chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from one of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Indeed, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, chose Islam as a religion for you, so improve your companionship with it through generosity and good character.
ai.seo_question: How should one demonstrate true companionship with Islam according to the Imams?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) emphasizes that Islam is not merely a set of rituals but a divine covenant requiring active, virtuous engagement. He instructs believers to 'companion' Islam through generosity (sakhā') and noble character (ḥusn al-khuluq), reflecting the Shia emphasis on the integration of inner faith with outward ethical conduct as a means of fulfilling the divine pleasure (irtidā').
